fact: Council router Phase 0 stack-detection canonical implementation lives in web/scripts/detect-stack.ts (exported `detectStack(workspaceRoot)` + `renderRefusal(result)` + closed-list constants `MARKER_NAMES` / `OVERRIDE_VALUES` / `REFUSAL_HEADLINES`). The three router SKILL.md files (~/.claude/skills/{council-plan,council-implement,council-review}/SKILL.md) are MIRROR artifacts whose drift is enforced by web/scripts/detect-stack.skill-mirror.test.ts (asserts each SKILL.md cites every MARKER_NAME + REFUSAL_HEADLINE + OVERRIDE_VALUE verbatim, AND that -aura/-copilot variants do NOT contain a Phase 0 section).
recommendation: To extend Phase 0 behavior: edit detect-stack.ts first (logic + new headline constants), then mirror SKILL.md to cite new strings verbatim. Skill-mirror canary turns red until both sides match. Do NOT attempt 'shared include' workarounds — the Claude Code harness has no SKILL.md include mechanism; the canary IS the drift discipline. The .council-stack-override file is the user-facing escape hatch, NOT a workaround for missing detection (depth=2 monorepo scan added 2026-06-01 to reduce override frequency).

fact: The New-Session model dropdown is now DYNAMIC (fact-006 was stale as of 2026-06-03). Claude list = live GET api.anthropic.com/v1/models keyed by settings.anthropicApiKey (web/server/anthropic-models-cache.ts, mem 1h + disk 24h cache ~/.companion/anthropic_models_cache.json, strict ^claude-[a-z0-9.\-]+$ id filter). Codex list = ~/.codex/models_cache.json written by the Codex CLI itself. web/server/model-registry.ts (~/.companion/models.json, bundled default constant) is a PURE annotate-only OVERLAY that can mark an already-listed model retired/blocked but NEVER adds ids. web/src/utils/backends.ts CLAUDE_MODELS/CODEX_MODELS remain the fallback when no key / upstream down.
recommendation: When a user asks 'why is model X missing/present in the dropdown': it is not a hardcode. A new model appears only if the source emits its id — Claude via /v1/models for the configured API key (else bundled fallback + subject to 1h/24h cache TTL; rotate key to force refresh), Codex via its own models_cache.json (update the CLI). The registry overlay only narrows. If the id genuinely does not exist upstream (e.g. a phantom 'fable 5'/'codex 5.5'), no config change surfaces it — verify existence before assuming a bug (see universal memory feedback_verify_upstream_version_exists_before_pin_bump).

fact: verifyProcessIdentity matches the exact `--sdk-url <sessionId>` argv token, so it returns kind:"mismatch" for any non-claude process (e.g. PTY shells)
recommendation: Before reusing verifyProcessIdentity for a new process class (terminals, codex, etc.), generalize it with an injected argv-shape predicate OR write a sibling verifyTerminalIdentity — never assume the helper is process-agnostic; it is fail-closed and will reject everything it wasn't built for

fact: PTY terminals in terminal-manager.ts use their own randomUUID-keyed instances Map (decoupled from the session Map) and are invisible to every existing cleanup sweep; their only reaper is an in-memory 5s orphanTimer lost on restart
recommendation: PTY shells (and docker-exec terminals) leak across server restarts. Any resource-reclamation work must add a sibling cleanup/terminal-orphan-reaper.ts + a persisted provenance sidecar for boot-reconcile; do NOT widen orphan-reaper.ts (which targets claude --sdk-url PPID=1 only). Docker terminals' proc.pid is the host-side docker-exec client, not the in-container shell

fact: prepareCodexHome (cli-launcher.ts) seeds per-session CODEX_HOME by copying ~/.codex/auth.json ONLY when dest is absent — a stale legacy auth.json poisons every NEW codex session.
recommendation: When new Codex sessions fail auth ('refresh token was already used'), check mtime of ~/.codex/auth.json under the service user; fix = codex login as that user, then create a NEW session (old session homes keep stale copies and won't recover). Structural risk: multiple live per-session auth.json copies refresh independently and invalidate each other's refresh tokens. Improvement candidate: re-seed auth.json when legacy file is newer than the copy.

fact: Uploaded-image base64 is NOT stored in the companion server messageHistory (it is stripped); it lives only in the Claude CLI transcript jsonl under a type:attachment / attachment.type:queued_command line in attachment.prompt[]
recommendation: To remove/fix a bad image from a live session: find newest-mtime jsonl in ~/.claude/projects/-root-<cwd>/ via grep -c '"base64"', back it up, edit the queued_command image block, then POST /api/sessions/<id>/relaunch (localhost bypasses auth) so the running --resume process re-reads it. Editing companion messageHistory does nothing

fact: Council pairs across projects have NO live cross-project message bus — they consume only two channels: their workspace .council/ filesystem (checkpoints/reviews) and git (commit->push->cross-host pull->restart). Linear/Slack are NOT read by running pairs.
recommendation: When proposing a handoff/notification to a live council pair, route via git or a direct REST prompt-inject (POST /api/sessions/<id>/message). Do NOT offer Linear/Slack as a way to reach a running pair: Linear is integrated but spawns SEPARATE Linear-agents (not the live pair) and Slack is only doc-level webhook examples, not a consumed channel. Those are human-facing surfaces only.

A separate install only appears if ITS server has telemetry enabled and the same COMPANION_STATS_URL. fact: Companion CLI-process reclamation is a 3-tier composition: boot orphan-reaper.ts (once, kills only UNtracked PPID=1 pids), daily eviction-sweeper.ts (Map/disk reclaim, kills ONLY archived+state==exited+identity-mismatch — deliberately RETAINS a matching live process), and daily archived-process-reclaim.ts (kills the live subprocess of archived+state!=exited sessions). The gap the third tier closes: an archived session whose subprocess is still alive+matching was killed by NONE of the others and leaked for weeks under KillMode=process (PPID=1)
recommendation: Before adding cleanup logic, place it in this taxonomy by responsibility axis: process-lifecycle (kill) vs Map/disk-entry reclaim. Don't widen an existing sweep across the axis — orphan-reaper targets untracked pids, eviction-sweeper owns Map/disk and retains live matching procs, archived-process-reclaim owns killing archived-but-alive. All three gate on evictionGrace.enabled and record to the shared cleanup-events store (EC-21).

fact: Aura Companion NEVER executes tools server-side; the CLI subprocess (Claude Code / Codex) owns its own tool loop and runs tools itself. The server only relays messages and gates permission approvals (codex-adapter proxies requestApproval -> browser -> JSON-RPC respond).
recommendation: Before speccing any new 'backend/provider' that is a bare inference API (no CLI), know that tool use requires a NET-NEW server-side tool-execution subsystem that does not exist today. Do not assume the provider seam gives you tools for free.
